claims.statement: The supplied Mississippi HO-3 2024-03 and DP-3 2026-01 base forms exclude loss caused by ordinance-or-law enforcement and compliance costs, while HO 04 16 editions modify the insurance for enforcement-related loss and control conflicting policy language within the endorsement's scope; HO 04 16 must not be assumed to amend DP-3 without an applicable attachment.

The supplied base forms have materially different built-in arrangements: DP-3 2026-01 provides the ordinance-or-law exclusion but no listed ordinance-or-law grant in its supplied Additional Coverages section; HO-3 2024-03 provides 15% of the amount of insurance applying to the dwelling in E.18 plus required demolition/reconstruction in E.19; HO-4 has no Coverage A despite an E.45 reference to 10% of Coverage A; HO-5 E.31 states 15% of the applicable amount of Coverage A; and HO-6 E.40 states additional coverage of 15% of Coverage A.

Both HO 04 16 editions require covered direct physical loss caused by a covered peril, an applicable ordinance or law in force and enforced by the responsible governmental authority, and a cost attributable to that covered loss; code-only loss, voluntary compliance, unrelated prior conditions, and elective betterment do not satisfy the stated coverage gates.

After the trigger is satisfied, HO 04 16 addresses loss in value or required demolition of an undamaged portion, required demolition and resulting debris removal, and the incremental cost to repair, rebuild, or replace covered property for compliance; the 2018 edition expressly enumerates building, safety, utility, accessibility, permit, inspection, and design-related work, while the 2023 edition excludes professional services unless directly required by the applicable ordinance or law and excludes dispute or appeal services.

HO 04 16 edition 2018-09 states a 10% of Coverage A ordinance-or-law limit and applies it to the total amounts payable under that coverage; it permits payment as work progresses or after completion when incurred costs are supported and permits withholding increased-construction-cost payment until covered construction is completed and compliance is evidenced.

HO 04 16 edition 2023-11 sets a 25% maximum for ordinance-or-law coverage tied to Coverage A property, applies one limit to the total covered costs rather than a separate limit per ordinance or law, permits covered code costs in addition to direct-physical-loss amounts without duplicate recovery, and requires repair or replacement at the same residence premises unless prohibited plus reasonable costs actually incurred for increased construction cost.

Both HO 04 16 editions apply a deductible only after covered ordinance-or-law loss is determined and require evidence of the governmental requirement, cost, and work; the editions require notice, records, inspection access, and supporting plans, permits, invoices, and evidence of incurred or completed work.

The 2023 HO 04 16 limit is tied to property insured under Coverage A and to the policy's Coverage A insurance, so its percentage cannot be assumed to transfer to a form that does not provide Coverage A, such as the supplied HO-4.

Roof settlement and ordinance-or-law coverage are separate: the roof must first have covered direct physical loss; HO-3 2024-03 applies its dwelling settlement basis to roof surfacing, while DP-3 2026-01 settles roof surfacing at actual cash value unless an actual-cash-value roof schedule endorsement is attached; HO 23 74 2025-05 settles roof surfacing at actual cash value at age twelve or more without itself creating or removing code coverage.

The supplied materials are Mississippi form editions, and DP-3 2026-01 provides that a provision required by applicable law controls over a conflicting policy term while the remaining policy term continues to the extent permitted by law; the water-loss handling guide is operational and noncontractual and therefore is not authority for deciding whether code-related costs are insured.

HO 04 16 is identified as an HO-3-line endorsement in both supplied editions; the 2018-09 edition remains relevant to policies written under it, while the 2023-11 edition governs its interval beginning 2023-11-01 when actually attached. Edition selection therefore depends on the policy interval and issued attachment rather than on the repository's newest file.

When HO 04 16 edition 2023-11 is attached to HO-3 2024-03, it modifies the base ordinance-or-law exclusion only within its stated coverage and controls a conflict for that coverage, while the base form and other unmodified provisions remain applicable.

The claims manual's ordinance-or-law chapter is an operational investigation sequence rather than contract authority: it directs confirmation of covered direct physical loss, separation of damaged and undamaged property, verification of the authority's requirement, and baseline-versus-compliant cost allocation, while the applicable form and attached endorsement control coverage.

The HO-3 2024-03 filing memorandum interprets the ordinance-or-law revision as clarifying the Coverage A relationship, the 15% limit, and the distinction between covered physical damage and compliance expense; it is interpretive and the filed HO-3 form controls if they differ.
